To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the somatogenic receptor and IGF-I m RNA are both expressed in rat liver parenchyma, whereas the IGF-I m RN A is expressed in non-paren chymal liver cells as well, but to a lesser extent.
somatogenic and IGF receptors are exclusively expressed in parenchyma, and IGF-1 mRNA predominantly, in comparison to a total non-parechymal cell population.
somatogenic receptors were only found in the parenchimial cell fraction and that IGF-I mRNA is expressed in both parenchymal (mainly) and non parenchymal liver cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the regulation of IGF-I synthesis in liver.
the regulation of the insulin-like growth factor (IGF) gene expression in the liver.
the study of the regulation of the synthesis of IGF-I by GH.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
GH is required to maintain IGF-I gene expression in liver parenchyme and that the IGF-I gene is also expressed in liver non-parenchyme, but to a lesser extent.
GH acts on the liver parenchyma through the somatogenic receptors to stimulate the synthesis of IGF-I and that the latter may act as a paracrine factor in liver.
GH acts through the liver, but not necessarily through IGF-I.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the GH-dependent expression of IGF-1 mRNA in liver is mediated via somatogenic receptors located in the parenchimal cells.
IGF-I is a major mediator of the growth-promoting action of GH in rat liver.
GH is the major regulator of IGF-I gene transcription in liver parenchimial cells and that this effect is mediated by the somatogenic receptor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
GH acts directly on liver parenchyma cells through somatogenic receptors to regulate the level of IGF-I.
the IGF-I receptor is expressed in both liver parenchyma and in non-parencymal liver cells.
the IGF-I system is expressed in liver parenchemal cells and non-parenchemal cells and that GH regulates this system in liver parenchemat cells.
